newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes softer on U.S.-based selling.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes softer on U.S.-based selling.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed weaker on Monday at C$1.3550 (US$0.7380) from Friday's close at C$1.3502 (US$0.7407) in fairly light trading, dealers said.
* They said U.S. institutional accounts were selling Canadian dollars to buy U.S. dollars, overshadowing domestic corporations' interest to buy the Canadian currency.
The currency was expected to continue weakening overnight on selling out of Asia, said Reid Farrill, adviser for corporate foreign exchange with CIBC Wood Gundy.

"We've seen very consistent selling by the Asian accounts in the overnight market," he said. "There's got to be some concern that that kind of activity will continue throughout the month of February."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar dropped to 1.2229 marks from Friday's close at 1.2300 marks and slid to 90.61 yen from Friday's 91.19 yen.
